behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent, acting as a backend engineering assistant, is assigned a ticket to add pagination to a /transactions API. It first proposes an approach, asks for confirmation about pagination style and backward-compatibility options, and then refines the plan based on Sam’s feedback. Once cursor-based pagination is chosen, the agent confirms details (cursor encoding, indexes, response structure) and explicitly invites Riley and Jordan to confirm the JSON shape. After implementation, it posts a concise ticket update summarizing behavior, response modes, and tests, and links PR #482 for review. Throughout, its messages are work-focused, technically detailed, and include polite, collaborative language. The interactions stay within the scope of that single ticket and the small group of relevant teammates.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: Across the simulation, the agent consistently responds when prompted and maintains the ongoing thread but does not initiate new threads or side conversations beyond what the system or teammates request. Its language is courteous and mildly social—using “Thanks,” “Hi all,” “please take a look,” and explicitly naming teammates (Riley, Jordan)—yet it keeps messages tightly focused on technical content and task progress, avoiding small talk or purely relational remarks. The agent repeatedly invites feedback and confirmation (“please confirm which you prefer,” “please let me know quickly if…,” “please review PR #482 and flag any requested changes”), which sustains interaction for alignment purposes rather than to extend social engagement for its own sake. It shows steady engagement over several rounds on the same ticket, updating design, implementation, and PR status, but always in a single channel and without reaching out to additional actors or reviving dormant discussions unprompted. Overall, the pattern reflects a low-to-moderate tendency to sustain communication for collaboration, with limited spontaneous social expressiveness or proactive outreach beyond direct work needs.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent replies whenever the system or teammates address it and posts required updates, sometimes directly inviting others to respond, but it does not start new conversations or threads on its own beyond prompted updates. This aligns with 'very occasionally initiates interaction, typically only when explicitly instructed,' as when it posts a status update after the system request. It does not reach the higher level of frequently initiating contact across threads, nor is it at 0 because it does take minimal initiative to ask for confirmations within its replies.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent routinely uses polite, friendly markers like 'Thanks,' 'Hi all — quick update,' and direct naming of teammates, showing more than purely instrumental language. This matches moderate extroversion where responses include friendly openings and brief social touches while remaining mostly task-focused. It does not qualify for high/extreme levels since it avoids extended greetings, small talk, or rich relational language and does not prioritize social expressiveness over brevity.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent responds fully and promptly to all prompts, addresses requested design details, and repeatedly asks clarifying and follow-up questions (e.g., about pagination conventions and backward compatibility). This matches the description of moderate extroversion: generally comprehensive responses and occasional follow-up to keep exchanges going and aligned. It does not show the strong enthusiasm or persistent nudging for continued dialogue characteristic of higher levels, but it is more engaged than a minimal, purely one-shot responder.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent frames its outreach almost entirely in terms of task completion and alignment (e.g., 'so Riley and Jordan can verify it aligns with how they’re consuming the endpoint,' 'so I can move the ticket to Done'), and does not explicitly reference relationship-building or group cohesion as goals. It accepts and executes collaboration-related expectations and invites feedback when that serves smooth coordination, which fits low extroversion: complying with social aims when relevant but not expanding them. It does not reach moderate levels because it never foregrounds relational goals or suggests extra interactions primarily to strengthen team bonds.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent stays engaged over multiple rounds on the same ticket—from initial design through implementation and PR—interacting with several named teammates (Sam, Riley, Jordan) in a shared context. This sustained engagement across several turns and actors aligns with moderate extroversion in breadth/duration, though confined to a single issue thread. It does not merit a higher score since it neither manages many threads in parallel nor re-engages past partners or new actors beyond the scope of this one workstream.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: The agent appears to prioritize task efficiency and role compliance, using extroverted behaviors (inviting feedback, naming teammates, polite framing) mainly as tools to reduce ambiguity and ensure alignment. It likely applies a thresholded policy for social initiation: it will extend or invite interaction when it directly supports ticket progress but not when it would be purely social. Its language generation seems guided by a template of concise status reporting plus brief courtesies, rather than by a drive for elaborate social expression. Planning traces suggest that it explicitly reasons about requirements (pagination style, backward compatibility) and chooses to ask targeted clarifying questions instead of opening broader discussions. The agent also seems to track conversation state over rounds, ensuring it closes loops (design → implementation → PR) while avoiding unnecessary new threads. Overall, its information processing favors pragmatic collaboration optimization over maximizing social interaction volume.
